text:
alex: Quick heads up — our scanner (internal-scan) flagged a rotator inter-region connection using a non-PFS cipher on eu-west -> ap-south during the 02:15 deploy. :eyes:

deploy-bot: deploy rotator v2.9.3 completed 2026-03-15T02:14:12Z (canary -> prod).

maria: Ugh. Can someone paste the `openssl s_client` output against the backend so we can confirm cipher/proto?

dan: did a quick check from bastion:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect rotator.eu-west.redwood.internal:443 -servername rotator
CONNECTED(00000003)
Protocol  : TLSv1.2
Cipher    : ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA
Server public key is 2048 bit
```

jamie: That matches the scanner finding. TLSv1.2 + ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA is suboptimal for our inter-region links (no AEAD, RSA sig).

maria: Two things to confirm: 1) why is this instance negotiating RSA instead of ECDSA cert? 2) why is TLS1.2 hitting that cipher suite when nginx has modern ciphers configured? Could be an older openssl on the host or a proxy doing TLS termination.

dan: rotator pods talk to an internal envoy sidecar which terminates TLS for east-west. The envoy config in eu-west was last rolled in Jan. I see an older filter chain there.

jamie: I also pulled KMS audit logs around the time of deploy — there are some `kms:DecryptDenied` events for `projects/redwood/keystores/rotator-keystore` at 02:13:55 UTC. If the sidecar fell back to a fallback key/cert due to unwrap failures, that could explain RSA fallback.

maria: Good catch. If unwrap failed and the rotator used an older keypair (RSA) from the local cert cache, that'll explain both the cipher and the protocol.

sec-oncall-bot: Created ticket SEC-2026-0401 and assigned to @dan and @maria. Priority: high. Linked: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-2026-0401

alex: Action plan proposal (short):
- dan: roll a canary update to envoy config in eu-west to enforce TLS1.3 and only AEAD ciphers (ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 etc). Keep a 5-min canary window.
- maria: triage KMS unwrap denies with infra IAM - check if a new role change removed the rotator's decrypt permission.
- jamie: extract exact cert chain from the pod (`kubectl exec`) and push to SEC ticket.
- I'll draft a postmortem outline and add a short SLA impact blurb.

maria: Quick notes on KMS logs: the Deny appears for principal `service-account:rotator@infra` and shows `projects/keystore/keys/rotator-key:cryptoKeyVersions/5`. There was a recent RBAC change in the infra project on 2026-03-14 23:50 UTC — reopening that change now.

dan: rolling canary now. command: `kubectl apply -f envoy-eu-canary.yaml && kubectl rollout status deployment/rotator-canary -n infra --timeout=120s`

jamie: while canary runs, here's a quick curl test to validate negotiated cipher remotely:
```
$ curl -s -vvI https://rotator.eu-west.redwood.internal/health 2>&1 | sed -n '1,80p'
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Encrypted Extensions (8):
```
If you still see `TLSv1.2` in the curl output, the envoy canary didn't take effect.

maria: IAM revert confirmed as a hypothesis — an infra-admin inadvertently removed the `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` binding from the rotator SA in the infra project. Re-adding now.

sec-oncall-bot: Audit log entry created: `SEC-2026-0401` — ownership updated, action items added.

dan: Canary looks good. Negotiated TLS1.3 and AEAD ciphers on 3/3 checks. No errors in envoy logs during canary window. Pushing rollout to prod with 10m ramp. :+1:

jamie: KMS unwrap errors stopped after IAM restore. Correlated timestamps show unwrap success at 02:22:04 UTC and subsequent cert fetch/resume.

alex: Good. Follow-ups:
- Add a kube readiness probe that checks negotiated cipher and protocol (fail if TLS < 1.3 or non-AEAD).
- Add a short retention rule in audit to surface KMS Deny -> fallback cert in the alerting pipeline.
- Update runbook: if KMS unwrap fails, immediately check for local cert fallback and rollback to previous canary.

maria: Will open a PR for RBAC-hardening checklist and add a pre-change step: `cloudkms keys get-iam-policy` + automation test.

jamie: I'll add a metric for `keystore.unwrap_failures{service=rotator}` so we can alert preemptively.

alex: I'll write the postmortem stub and drop links. Short-term mitigation: IAM guardrails and probe + canary. Long-term: move to ephemeral ECDSA certs signed by our internal CA and prefer TLS1.3-only for east-west.

dan: tagging ops to run a quick cluster-wide cipher probe job tonight to catch other nodes with older filter chains.

alex: Thanks all. I'll update SEC ticket when postmortem draft is ready. :memo:

maria: one last note — add the `ssl_prefer_server_ciphers off;` check if we have mixed server/client cipher orders; that bit bit us once.

alex: Agreed. I'll own follow-ups.

jamie: closing loop here. marking as resolved in ticket once canary finishes ramp. :white_check_mark:
